draft.title: The October Days
card: By October 1789 Paris had a bread shortage and prices were high. Many women who bought and sold food in the markets were angry and hungry.
On 5 October thousands of Parisian women marched about 20 kilometres to Versailles, where the king lived. They demanded bread and were joined by National Guardsmen under Lafayette.

The crowd also pressed the king to accept the August decrees and the Declaration of the Rights of Man. Some crowd members broke into the palace, and on 6 October the royal family agreed to move to Paris.
The royal family settled in the Tuileries Palace. The king was now close to the people of Paris, and the Assembly soon followed him there.
draft.remember: Hungry Parisian women forced the king from Versailles to Paris, and showed that crowds could shape the revolution.

a.q: What was the main reason the women of Paris marched to Versailles on 5 October 1789?
opts: Bread was scarce and dear, and they wanted the king to act
They wanted the Assembly to abolish the monarchy
They wanted to free prisoners held at the palace
They wanted the king to lead an army against Austria
a.why: The march began with food shortages and high bread prices, and the women took their demands to the king. The monarchy was not abolished until 1792, so a call to end it in 1789 is wrong.
a.clue: Think about what market women needed to buy each day.

b.q: Marie says the October Days were only a food protest with no political result. Which fact from the events best challenges her view?
opts: The royal family was brought from Versailles to Paris
The crowd marched about 20 kilometres in the rain
The women were joined by National Guardsmen
The march began over a shortage of bread
b.why: Moving the royal family to Paris placed the king near the people and changed the balance of power, so the result was political. Bread shortages were the cause, and they support Marie's view rather than challenge it.
b.clue: Look for an outcome, not a cause.

a.best: Bread was scarce and dear, and they wanted the king to act

b.best: The royal family was brought from Versailles to Paris

problems.detail: The remember line says the women 'forced' the king to Paris, but the card says the crowd 'pressed' him and the royal family 'agreed to move'. The remember line is stronger than the card.

The right option stands out. It is the longest and the only one that does not begin 'They wanted', and the other options are implausible. The clue about what market women bought each day all but names bread, so the question is too easy for Year 12.
The distractor 'about 20 kilometres in the rain' includes the rain, which the card never mentions. The detail is historically true but is not taught here.

proposal.remember: Hunger drove Parisian women to Versailles, and pressure from the crowd moved the king and the Assembly to Paris.

a.q: What was the main cause of the women's march to Versailles on 5 October 1789?
opts: Scarce, costly bread that left many families hungry
Anger that the king had shut down the National Assembly
Fear that the king was about to flee from Paris
A plan to end the monarchy and set up a republic
a.why: The march grew out of a bread shortage and high prices, and the women went to demand bread. The Assembly still existed and soon followed the king to Paris, so it had not been shut down. The king lived at Versailles, not Paris, and he stayed king after the move.
a.clue: Think about conditions in Paris before the march.

The march began over a shortage of bread
b.why: Moving the royal family to Paris placed the king near the people and the Assembly followed, which changed the balance of power. Bread shortages were the cause of the march, so they support Marie's view rather than challenge it.
b.clue: Look for an outcome, not a cause.

a.best: Scarce, costly bread that left many families hungry

b.best: The royal family was brought from Versailles to Paris
